transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I guess… it’s my eating. Some evenings after work, especially if I’ve been really strict with myself all day, I end up eating a lot more than I meant to. Like dinner, then cereal or crackers, leftovers, sweets… all within a couple hours. It’s embarrassing.
During these times when you end up eating more than you meant to, do you feel like you’re not in control of what or how much you’re eating?
Yeah… I think so. Once I start, I keep going back to the kitchen even though I’m telling myself to stop. I don’t really feel like I’m back in control until I’m… too full.
After these episodes of eating more than you intended, do you ever try to make up for it by making yourself sick, using laxatives, or exercising a lot more than usual?

I don’t usually make myself sick or anything like that. But… the next day I’ll try to make up for it, I guess. Like skipping breakfast and lunch, or going on a really long hike, or pushing harder at softball conditioning even if I’m tired.
Do you often engage in behaviors like fasting, excessive exercise, or strict dieting specifically to try to control your weight or compensate for the food you’ve eaten after these episodes?

Yeah… I guess I do. The next day I’ll tell myself I’m making up for it, so I’ll skip breakfast and lunch, or do an extra-long hike. Sometimes I push harder at softball conditioning too, even if I’m already tired.
Do these episodes of eating a lot happen within a short period of time, like a couple of hours, and do they usually cause you a lot of distress or upset?

Yeah… it’s usually in an evening, within a couple hours. Like after work, especially if I’ve been really strict all day, I’ll have dinner and then keep going—cereal, crackers, leftovers, sweets. It does upset me, yeah.
